questions.stem: A neurologist met with a male person of age 23 years who had the high capability to retain information about the phone numbers which were revised several times in an event. The person was able to interpret the phone number easily. Neurologists concluded that a person has Good capability of which type of memory?

options.label: A
options.text: Long-term memory

options.label: B
options.text: Working memory

options.label: C
options.text: Short-term memory

options.label: D
options.text: All incorrect

questions.solutionHtml:
Short-term memory
  • Short-term memory also called primary or active memory is the capacity for holding, but not manipulating, a small amount of information in mind in an active, readily available state for a short period.
  • For example, short-term memory can be used to remember a phone number that has just been recited. The duration of short-term memory (when rehearsal or active maintenance is prevented) is believed to be in the order of seconds.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology 14th Edition, Page No. 736.

questions.stem: Neurologists studied the role of Memory traces in all parts of the brain and concluded the presence of memory traces in the spinal cord. Select the incorrect memory traces:

options.label: A
options.text: Theoretical means by which memories are physically stored in the brain.

options.label: B
options.text: Memory traces can be selectively activated by the thinking mind to reproduce the memories.

options.label: C
options.text: Most memories with intellectual processes are based on memory traces in the cerebral cortex.

options.label: D
options.text: Most memories in the brain are associated with the cerebellum.

questions.answerText: Most memories in the brain are associated with the cerebellum.
questions.solutionHtml:
Most memories in the brain are associated with the cerebellum.
Most memories with intellectual processes are based on memory traces in the cerebral cortex.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology,14th Edition, Page No. 736.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old male was taken to the hospital with manifestations of impaired thinking, impaired behavior, muscle rigidity, impaired movement of hands, and mood changes over the past several months. Examination revealed the presence of abnormal deposits of a protein called alpha-synuclein in the brain. Some facial expressions in the image signify the manifestations. The patient was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. Select the incorrect:

options.label: A
options.text: Impaired ability to hit and see a tennis ball.

options.label: B
options.text: Impaired ability to perceive the relationship and speed of the ball to the racquet

options.label: C
options.text: Impaired ability to deduce rapidly the motions of the body, the arms, and the racquet required to hit the ball as desired

options.label: D
options.text: Declarative memory

questions.solutionHtml:
Declarative memory

Skill memory is affected in persons with Lewy body dementia, and Parkinson's disease. Declarative memory or explicit memory is devoted to the processing of names, dates, places, facts, events, and so forth. These are entities that are thought of as being encoded symbolically and that thus can be described with language. In terms of function, declarative memory is specialized for fast processing and learning.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology,14th Edition, Page No. 736.

questions.stem: Neurologists studied that sensations like pain or pleasure, the brain has a different automatic capability of enhancing and storing memory traces. In this way, the brain is capable of processing positive and negative memories in one’s life. Select the Correct Option:

options.label: A
options.text: The brain has the capability to avoid information of no value by inhibiting the synaptic pathways.

options.label: B
options.text: Habituation is a type of negative memory.

options.label: C
options.text: Positive memory by facilitation of the synaptic pathways.

options.label: D
options.text: All of them

questions.solutionHtml:
All of them
  • Positive memory is stored by the facilitation of the synaptic pathways.
  • The brain is inundated with sensory information from all our senses. If our minds attempted to remember all this information, the memory capacity of the brain would be rapidly exceeded.
  • Fortunately, the brain has the capability to ignore information that is of no consequence. This capability results from the inhibition of the synaptic pathways for this type of information; the resulting effect is called habituation, which is a type of negative memory.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 736.

questions.stem: A patient at the age of 23 years reported to the psychiatrist about the habit of washing his hands repeatedly. The psychiatrist did counseling of the patient by addressing that it is an abnormal habituation that can be dropped by counseling and medication. You should not panic about it. Select the incorrect mechanism of habituation:

options.label: A
options.text: Progressive closure of calcium channels through the terminal membrane leads to a habituation effect in the sensory terminal.

options.label: B
options.text: Habituation is a negative memory.

options.label: C
options.text: Habituation is skill memory.

options.label: D
options.text: Correct A and B

questions.solutionHtml:
Correct A and B
  • Option A. Progressive closure of calcium channels through the terminal membrane leads to a habituation effect in the sensory terminal.
  • Option B. Habituation is a negative memory- At the molecular level, the habituation effect in the sensory terminal results from the progressive closure of calcium channels through the terminal membrane, although the cause of this calcium channel closure is not fully known. Nevertheless, much smaller than normal amounts of calcium ions can diffuse into the habituated terminal, and much less sensory terminal transmitter is therefore released because calcium entry is the principal stimulus for transmitter release.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 736-738.

questions.stem: In a class of research scholars of neurology, the neurologist was teaching the basics of neural Facilitation. He explained the role of calcium ions in the neural facilitation process. Select the incorrect option:

options.label: A
options.text: Serotonin is released at the facilitator synapse on the surface of the sensory terminal.

options.label: B
options.text: Adenyl cyclase causes the formation of cyclic adenosine monophosphate inside the sensory presynaptic terminal.

options.label: C
options.text: cAMP activates a protein kinase and blocks potassium channels causing a prolonged action potential.

options.label: D
options.text: Prolonged action potential suppresses calcium channels for a long period.

questions.answerText: Prolonged action potential suppresses calcium channels for a long period.
questions.solutionHtml:
Prolonged action potential suppresses calcium channels for a long period.

The prolonged action potential does not suppress calcium channels for a long period but activates calcium channels.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 737.

questions.stem: A patient at age 56 years visited the physician with manifestations of difficulty falling asleep at night, tiredness in the morning, and ill feeling of depression state from the past 6 months. The patient was diagnosed with insomnia. Select the incorrect memory:

options.label: A
options.text: A time-dependent process by which recently learned experiences are transformed into long-term memory.

options.label: B
options.text: Insomnia causes failure of consolidation of memory.

options.label: C
options.text: Deep general anesthesia can temporarily block the consolidation of memory.

options.label: D
options.text: All of them are incorrect

questions.solutionHtml:
All of them are incorrect

Memory consolidation is a category of processes that stabilize a memory trace after its initial acquisition.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 737.

questions.stem: A patient at the age of 59 years came to the physician with an inability to remember the house number, name of the street, and names of his friend whom he met recently. He gave H/O surgical removal of both hippocampi for epilepsy treatment. The patient was diagnosed with anterograde amnesia. Select the incorrect:

options.label: A
options.text: Absence of capability for storing verbal and symbolic types of declarative memory.

options.label: B
options.text: No capability to retain skill memory.

options.label: C
options.text: Hippocampus is involved in the “reward” and “punishment” areas of the limbic system.

options.label: D
options.text: “Reward” and “punishment” together provide the background mood and motivations for all persons.

questions.answerText: No capability to retain skill memory.
questions.solutionHtml:
No capability to retain skill memory.
  • Skill memory is procedural memory, also called implicit memory, and is a type of long-term memory involved in the performance of different actions and skills. Essentially, it is the memory of how to do certain things.
  • Riding a bike, tying shoes, and cooking without a recipe are all examples of procedural memories.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 738-739.

questions.stem: The memory formation process in the CNS involves all except:

options.label: A
options.text: It involves a change in neurotransmitter release at the synapse.

options.label: B
options.text: Increase in no. of synapses and dendrites.

options.label: C
options.text: Recruitment of neurons and involvement of more neurons in a particular function as in the somatosensory area of the cortex.

options.label: D
options.text: Allocation of specialized nerve cells occurs in the hippocampus.

questions.answerText: Allocation of specialized nerve cells occurs in the hippocampus.
questions.solutionHtml:
Allocation of specialized nerve cells occurs in the hippocampus.

Allocation of specialized nerve cells doesn't occur in the hippocampus.

Being an integral part of the limbic system, the hippocampus plays a vital role in regulating learning, memory encoding, memory consolidation, and spatial navigation.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology,14 Edition, Page No. 738-739.

questions.stem: Which of the following is excitatory?

options.label: A
options.text: Gamma-amino-butyric acid

options.label: B
options.text: Glycine

options.label: C
options.text: Glutamate

options.label: D
options.text: Lysine

questions.solutionHtml:
Glutamate

The amino acid glutamate is the main excitatory neurotransmitter in the brain and spinal cord and may be responsible for 75% of the excitatory transmission in the CNS.




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 656
